text: Inference (Anumāna) is the process of arriving at a conclusion (Anumiti). Knowledge arising from associative reasoning (Paramarśa) is a conclusion. Knowledge of the presence of a property in the subject, characterized by invariable concomitance (Vyāpti), is associative reasoning. For example, the knowledge that "this mountain is smoky, and smoke is pervaded by fire" is associative reasoning. The knowledge resulting from this, that "the mountain possesses fire," is the conclusion. The rule of association that "wherever there is smoke, there is fire" is invariable concomitance. The presence of the pervaded (smoke) on the mountain is the presence of the property in the subject (Pakṣadharmatā).
